data.narrative:
Cache Energy is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Arpit Dwivedi that has raised $8.5M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though a sufficiently tight peer set at the same stage and valuation tier does not exist to support median-based valuation.

Given the nascent peer universe at Seed stage within this sector, the Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. This method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $8M raised proxy, reflecting typical progression economics from Seed to subsequent financing rounds. This yields an implied valuation of $21M. A sensitivity band around this point estimate—accounting for variance in step-up magnitude and earlier-stage risk—supports a range of $18M (low) to $24M (high).

The analysis supports a median valuation of $21M with a reasonable range of $18M–$24M. The primary uncertainty is the absence of narrow-stage peer data; the stage-progression method relies on historical step-up multiples rather than direct comparable transaction evidence. A fuller peer set—either through additional Seed-stage closings in climate tech or adjacent subsector data—would strengthen conviction in this range. Current raised capital and founder pedigree provide the floor; execution risk and market timing for the next round represent the key downside and upside vectors.
